pageCache.text:
Welcome
Welcome to the Harlyn Primary School website
The school is situated in the north of the London Borough of Hillingdon bordering Pinner. Harlyn is a two-form entry primary school with a Nursery in Northwood Hills. I know that choosing the right school for your child is an important decision for parents to make and I believe I have a dedicated and experienced staff of teachers and support staff who work together as a strong team, to give the children the maximum opportunity to achieve, prepare them for the future and have fun. We have six acres of attractive grounds, landscaped with trees and shrubs, a large playground, two spacious sports fields, and a conservation area (See the link below). At Harlyn Primary School we strive to develop the individual talents of our children, and encourage their motivation towards good standards of academic work and behaviour. We want all our children to be happy and successful at school. The involvement of parents in all aspects of school life is actively encouraged (See the link below). The school year is shaped to include opportunities for musical presentations, drama, celebration, involvement in the local community and visits by speakers and performers. We set particular value on the tolerance and understanding of all faiths and on building a community of genuinely equal opportunity. We offer a wide variety of extra curricular activities which regularly includes a large number of sports, music clubs and other clubs. If you would like to visit the school please contact the school office and I would be very pleased to meet with you and show you around. I hope you find all the information on this website useful.

Meet the Governors
Welcome to the Governors' section!
Here is list of our current Governors.
Sally de Jongh (Chair)
Michele Matonti (Vice Chair)
Should you wish to email the governors please use: clerk@harlynprimaryschool.co.uk
For a copy of the signed Governing Board minutes, please contact the Clerk as above.
It has been my privilege to have been a member of the Harlyn governing body for sixteen years. Both my daughters
attended the school from the nursery upwards, and then moved on to Watford Grammar school for girls. One is currently in her third year of university, and the other preparing for her A levels for next Spring.
I am retired but did work within Local Authority for many years so do have some knowledge of ‘how it works!’
I am available during the day and can be quite busy attending various sub committee meetings and sitting on interview panels, for both teaching and non-teaching staff.
Harlyn is a very happy school where the children are cared for and educated well, and we have an excellent senior management team.
My special interests within the school are with our SEN department, Safeguarding and Child Protection.
I have watched this department grow until we now are hugely respected for our provision for SEN children.
The Governing Board is very dedicated in its strategic role within the school and we will continue to work together with the
Head Teacher to ensure Harlyn continues to be a successful school where parents will continue to want their children educated.
Long-serving Governor nominated by the Local Education Authority. Father of three, who were educated in the Eastcote / Northwood Hills area, and grandfather to five. Worked as a principal research scientist at Kodak in Wealdstone, now retired. Very aware of the importance of the best education for children of all abilities, and keen to support Harlyn in achieving this. Academic background is in the sciences and maths, other interests include the natural world, walking, travelling, sailing, the local community and local politics.
Is married with two children who are currently teenagers. She is an IT consultant and a professional with an immense amount of experience. She has previously worked in a professional services company which is number one in the world and currently works with Lloyds Banking Group.
Abi is passionate about young people fulfilling their purpose no matter their background, she is currently studying a Masters'
program in Applied Anthropology, Community and Youth Work. She is passionate about serving and enjoys her role as a School Governor utilising her IT knowledge.
had a daughter in the school and lives locally to Harlyn Primary School. Murray is a consultant advising on media regulation and age-verification, Director at 18North, and an advisory board member for an age-verification and digital ID company.
Murray's background in media regulation includes twenty years with the British Board of Film Classification, leading work to
implement online protections, and film classification in his native New Zealand. Murray continues to support measures to
improve online safety, both in the UK and abroad, so that our children can benefit from the best of the online world while
being protected from the worst of it.
As a parent and local resident, Murray is a strong believer in helping our school and its students achieve their potential and
values the opportunity to contribute as a Governor.
I have one child who currently attends Harlyn Primary School and have always been grateful for the hard work, expertise and passion that goes into my children’s education. I hope to be able to bring some of my experience to the school to support and help where I can, and the role of Governor gives that ambition the framework and context to do so. I have worked in the property industry for most of my career and enjoy working in, and managing, teams in some interesting, challenging and fun projects and hope to bring come of that into my interactions with the school staff too.
My past 7 years at Harlyn have taught me the importance of teamwork and having a strong sense of school community which is what I strive to implement into my everyday practice amongst staff and pupils alike.
My past career as a chef instilled the value of hard work and multi-tasking which helps with my current roles as Class Teacher, PE Lead and Staff Governor.
As PE Lead, I am actively involved in planning a plethora of events throughout the year as I strive to give children a variety of opportunities.
Abi Walton - Parent Governor
As a dedicated parent, I am committed to supporting our school's nurturing and inclusive environment. Becoming a Governor allows me to contribute to school improvement and uphold the high educational standards.
With experience in finance, universities, and leadership, I bring problem-solving, strategic planning, and teamwork skills to help our school thrive.
Glenn Smith - Parent Governor
I have served in the Royal Air Force for fifteen years in Geospatial Intelligence as an “Air Cartographer”. With experience in Quality Assurance and championing personal development, I completed a master’s degree in Education, coaching, mentoring and leadership and bring a passion for education to my role as a School Governor. I am dedicated to promoting STEAM subjects, inspiring young minds to develop problem-solving skills and a lifelong love for learning. With a strong focus on fostering a growth mindset, I support initiatives that build self-confidence, resilience, and perseverance in children. My experience in mentoring and leadership enables me to contribute effectively to the school’s strategic development and the success of its pupils.

Admissions (Nursery)
At Harlyn we have our own purpose built Nursery, with its own play areas. It caters for 30 children per morning and 15 for afternoon sessions. Morning sessions are 8.30-11.30 and afternoon sessions are 12.30-3.30.
It is run by a Nursery Teacher, Nursery Nurse and Nursery Assistants, one being a qualified first aider. Children attend the Nursery from the age of three years. If the nursery is not full in the September intake, the school will consider a January intake of that academic year.
The learning environment is organised to enable the children to have learning opportunities in all seven areas of the curriculum, which are:-
We offer equal opportunities for all children and foster an understanding amongst children that all people should be equally valued within a secure, challenging and stimulating environment, where children develop a positive self image, self confidence and concern for others. Harlyn Nursery offers appropriate encouragement and praise to support all children in the acquisition of knowledge, understanding, skills and attitudes.
We encourage parents/carers to be actively involved in the learning process and respect their status as the child's first educators.
We currently offer the free 30 hours places to parents/carers who are eligible. Children can attend from 8.30am to 2.30pm using the free 30 hours, or parents/carers can pay for an additional hour until 3.30pm at a cost of £7 per day. Parents/carers who do not qualify are able to pay for additional hours themselves.
The current fees are £7.00 for the lunch hour, £21 until 2.30pm (which includes the lunch hour) or £28 for the afternoon session until 3.30pm, which includes the lunch hour. Fees are reviewed annually.
Parents can apply for a place in Harlyn's Reception class in September after their fourth birthday via Hillingdon Council. There is only one intake per year into the Reception Class.

Parental Information
As a Harlyn parent we hope you will work in partnership with us to support your child's learning. Like you we want the best for your child and by working together we can ensure your child's needs will be met and supported.
We encourage parents to get involved in school activities and we value any support and help you can give us. You are encouraged to join our class assemblies on most Thursdays and Key Stage One birthday assemblies on Fridays.
The children benefit from parent's assistance in food technology, reading, library duties, sewing, sports and visits.
We have two open evenings a year when you have the opportunity to meet your child's teacher and view your child's work. End of year reports are issued in July.
Daily contact with class teachers is generally available after school. You are always welcome to make an appointment with the Headteacher to discuss any concerns.
You are invited to various activities during the year including curriculum evenings, concerts and sports events.
All parents are members of the Fund Raising Association, which has charitable status. A committee composed of parents and staff regularly arrange a programme of events, in order to raise additional funds for the school and to encourage parents and families to meet together. Recent events have included Summer Funshine, Christmas Fair and Happy Circus.
The success of these events is due to the tremendous support of parents and staff.
Do come and join us !
